newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha extends losses in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha extends losses in quiet trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices lost ground for the third consecutive day on Friday due to softer European markets combined with ample prompt supplies in the region, traders said.
"It's mainly weak markets in Europe, but fundamentals are not so strong either," one naphtha dealer said.
Discussion remained thin through the day with the Singapore market closed for a public holiday.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was quoted at around $203.00/204.00 per tonne. It was said to have been traded at $207.50 on Thursday.
In spreads, first-half June/first-half July was traded at minus $3.00 on Thursday, indicating the first-half June contract was valued $3.00 per tonne lower than first-half of July.

Saudi Aramco is expected to notify Asian traders who participated in the first round of bidding for naphtha cargoes to be lifted in the July-December period of the schedule for face-to-face negotiations, traders said.
The talks are expected to be held in Singapore or Tokyo later this month or early next month, they added.
